title: How to spot a kingfisher in 3 steps

scenes.headline: Scan perches near water
scenes.body: Lakes, ponds, streams, wetlands: check low branches, reeds and even wires along the bank.

scenes.headline: Listen for a long, trilling 'chee-chee'
scenes.body: In flight a common kingfisher is so fast it looks like a blue blur, so use your ears.

scenes.headline: Wait. It hunts from the perch.
scenes.body: It watches the water and dives when a fish swims close. Pied kingfishers, like this one, also hover first.

caption:
Three steps, no gear needed.

A common kingfisher is only about 17 cm long, which is why it is so easy to miss on a busy riverbank. Pied kingfishers do something most kingfishers don't: they can swallow small fish in flight.

Source: Animal Diversity Web (Alcedo atthis; Ceryle rudis).  Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Numbered how-to with one field skill and three steps, each matched to a real clip (common and pied kingfisher); steps come from species accounts, not generic tips.
